name: dual
comment: Step-1 anchor plus a full-horizon secondary slot, gate off.
Continues the mine rather than starting beside it. The rollout schedule makes
every epoch where (epoch - 1) is a multiple of the config's hdp_rollout_interval
a refresh epoch that re-samples the whole corpus, so epoch 1 belongs to the mine
arm and this one starts at epoch 2 -- starting it at 1 would throw away the
buffer that was just mined and pay to mine it again.
Both switches resolve out of the mine's output directory, so there is no stamp to
copy by hand: the mine writes a single epoch_001.pth and this reads it. That
checkpoint carries a live policy and an optimizer, so the two inherited resume
switches apply unchanged -- the mine takes no optimizer step, so what they
restore is the base model's own state.
A refresh epoch clears the buffer and re-samples the SAME scene list with the
current policy, into this run's own cache directory rather than truncating the one
it resumed from. So a refresh buys fresher candidate trajectories, not more scenes,
and it charges a full mine of wall-clock during which no optimizer step is taken
plus a second buffer's worth of disk that lives until the run ends. The interval
set here is larger than any epoch budget, so none fires and every epoch is a
gradient epoch: the anchor term regresses on the logged trajectory, which no
refresh can make fresher, and it is the term that moves the executed waypoint.
Do not lower it below the epoch count to buy a refresh: a refresh epoch puts the
arm back on the mining path, which scores group-relative and therefore refuses the
candidate weighting this arm exists to apply. Preflight rejects that combination
rather than letting it abort every rank once the refresh epoch arrives. To sample
fresher candidates, mine again with the mine spec and resume from the new buffer.
To continue an interrupted run, point both switches at runs/dual instead; that is
what the runner's --supervise does on every relaunch.
